text: {"question":"What change in the inferred value of the Hubble constant is reported between the earlier and later studies, and how does the newer analysis address the tension with the Planck measurement?","reference_answer":"The earlier work reports an elevated Hubble constant around 70 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, while the later study finds a value consistent with the Planck 2018 result of 67.36 ± 0.54 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ in its preferred TGPAge‑Fix model, thereby reducing or resolving the Hubble tension.","passage_1_contribution":"Earlier study notes an increased H0 (~70 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹) when including SIdr, which helps alleviate but does not eliminate the tension.","passage_2_contribution":"Later study shows TGPAge‑Fix yields H0 consistent with Planck’s 67.36 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹, thus naturally alleviating the tension.","joint_reason":"Both passages discuss the Hubble constant and its relation to the Planck measurement, with the newer analysis providing a value that aligns more closely with Planck and thereby addressing the tension.","same_quantity":true}
